title: Super Heroes vs. Super Villains
description: Create JavaScript classes that model super humans, heroes, and villains and determine the winner of a battle.

instructions.studentPrompt:
Complete hero.js by defining three JavaScript classes: SuperHuman, SuperHero, and SuperVillain.

Requirements:

- Create a SuperHuman class.
- The SuperHuman constructor must have exactly two parameters: name and powerLevel.
- The SuperHuman constructor must assign name and powerLevel to properties with the same names.
- Create a SuperHero class that extends SuperHuman.
- The SuperHero constructor must have exactly three parameters: name, alias, and powerLevel.
- The SuperHero constructor must call the parent constructor with name and powerLevel.
- The SuperHero constructor must assign alias to an alias property.
- Add a battle() method to SuperHero that accepts a SuperVillain object.
- battle() must return true when the hero's powerLevel is greater than or equal to the villain's powerLevel.
- battle() must return false when the hero's powerLevel is less than the villain's powerLevel.
- Create a SuperVillain class that extends SuperHuman.
- The SuperVillain constructor must have exactly three parameters: name, alias, and powerLevel.
- The SuperVillain constructor must call the parent constructor with name and powerLevel.
- The SuperVillain constructor must assign alias to an alias property.
- Add a getEvilChuckle() method to SuperVillain.
- getEvilChuckle() must return exactly "Ha ha ha!".
- Define the classes in the global scope so index.js and the webpage can use SuperHero and SuperVillain.
